issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning a String and that feedAllAnimals() should call messageOnFeed() and print the message. The solution implementation, however, changes the return type to FeedResponse (a custom class) for Animal.messageOnFeed() and concrete animals (Seal, Pig, Goat) return FeedResponse instances. This structural change conflicts with the exercise specification and the expected simple String return, and would confuse students implementing the method according to the problem/UML (they will declare messageOnFeed() to return String), making the solution and tests incompatible with the stated API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by changing Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String (not FeedResponse). Remove or stop using the FeedResponse class, and update all concrete implementations (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the corresponding String messages (e.g. "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intentionally required, update the problem statement, UML, and template to document and expect FeedResponse as the return type so students are not misled.

issues.description: The problem statement requires Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a String (messageOnFeed():String), but the solution defines and uses a FeedResponse class as the return type (Animal.messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse). This introduces a different identifier (FeedResponse) for the feed-message concept compared to the problem description and will confuse students about the expected return type of messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the feed message consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (update Animal, Seal, Pig, Goat to return String and remove or adapt FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify FeedResponse as the expected return type and document its fields/behavior. Prefer option (A) to match the original exercise description.
